speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Let's begin by clarifying your sudden-onset vertigo: does this sensation of spinning last for seconds or does it persist for hours, and did it start while you were lying down or moving your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: BPPV (Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo). The clinical picture of sudden-onset spinning lasting about three minutes, triggered by the maneuver of going to bed, is classic for BPPV. I will now request a Dix-Hallpike test to confirm the presence of posterior canal nystagmus before proceeding with treatment.
